Subject: Follow-up: PII handling for prompts & outputs (recap + next steps)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. As promised, a short written recap of how Redwood handles prompt and output data, plus the configurable options we discussed. This should help your security and legal teams triage next steps.

Summary (hosted Redwood API):
- What we store by default:
  - Prompts: transiently logged for debugging and quality for a configurable retention window (default 30 days). Stored encrypted at rest.
  - Model outputs: logged only if "log_outputs" is enabled for the project (off by default for strict data use cases). When enabled, outputs follow the same retention policy as prompts.
  - System and access logs: audit logs (control plane events, API access) are retained separately for compliance (default retention 180 days, configurable).
- Where data is stored:
  - By default data is stored in the customer project region; for hosted customers we can pin storage to US (us-west-2) or EU (eu-central-1) as part of an enterprise contract.
- Retention options:
  - Default: 30 days for prompt/output logs (configurable to any value including 0 days for no retention).
  - Debug captures: may be retained longer if explicitly approved (we require an internal ticket and customer approval).
- Controls & safeguards:
  - Encryption at rest and in transit (KMS-backed keys; customer-managed keys available on Dedicated/Private).
  - Role-based access control and audit trails for who accessed logs.
  - SOC 2 Type II and regular penetration testing; we provide artifacts on request (DPA/Security Whitepaper).
  - Optional redaction/scrubbing: customer-side SDK redaction or server-side prompt-scrubbing rules (regex-based) can be applied before storage.

Private & Dedicated deployment notes:
- Dedicated: logs remain in your dedicated GPU pool and can be configured to not persist prompts/outputs beyond ephemeral caches.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer has full control — Redwood control plane can be run in-region and you can choose not to store prompts/outputs at all.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review the attached one-page summary for your legal/security team ("Redwood-PII-handling-summary.pdf").
2) If BrightPath needs EU-only residency, we can provision an EU-hosted project (requires enterprise agreement).
3) Schedule a short technical workshop with Marissa to validate retention/retention-0, redaction rules, and any required SLA/DPA changes.

Please confirm whether the above aligns with your notes from today and share any additional constraints (e.g., required retention = 0 days, or whether debug captures must be explicitly opt-in via a signed form).

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Elena — answers inline below. I’ll also attach an expanded config spreadsheet that maps settings to behavior.

1) Control plane / analytics:
- Prompts and outputs for a customer project are stored only in the project storage (customer tenant) and are not routed to a global analytics store that contains prompt text. We do collect aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts) but that telemetry does not include raw prompt text.
- For enterprise customers we can scope control plane logs to a specific region (EU) as part of the enterprise onboarding.

2) Redaction:
- Yes: server-side scrubbing is supported. We provide two options:
  a) Managed scrubber: regex-based rules you provide; applied immediately before storage.
  b) Client-side SDK redaction helpers: perform PII redaction in your application before sending.
- For strict PII use cases we recommend client-side redaction + server-side scrubber as a defense-in-depth approach.

3) 0-day retention + debug captures:
- Hosted: default retention is 30 days, but we support 0-day retention (no persistence) for prompts/outputs for production traffic if requested in the enterprise contract.
- Debug captures can be enabled on a per-capture basis and require explicit customer approval; we can enforce auto-expiry (e.g., 7 days) for any debug capture. That will be documented in the DPA/tech addendum.

4) EU residency:
- Yes — we have EU-hosted projects (eu-central-1) available for enterprise customers that include prompt/output storage and audit logs within the EU region. Note: provisioning EU-hosted projects typically requires an enterprise agreement and declaration of region.

Security artifacts & next steps:
- I'll attach the config spreadsheet (BrightPath-prompt-output-config.xlsx) and send our Security Whitepaper and DPA link to Legal.
- Proposed next step: schedule a 60-min technical workshop where Marissa walks through configuration toggles (retention, scrubbers, KMS). Is early next week good?

Thanks,
Rishi
